Holzbaurechner / Wine crate

Wooden wine crate calculator

A wooden box in the style of a classic wine crate, for display, planting, gifts or as a shelf. Enter the outside size and you get every part in centimetres.

How the wine crate is built

The two ends are solid end pieces 18 mm thick. The thin side boards, 10 mm thick, are nailed or screwed to them, with the bottom boards underneath. That keeps the crate light but sturdy. To avoid gaps, the calculator spreads the height evenly over the boards and tells you what width to rip them to.

The end pieces get hand holes: drill two holes with a Forstner bit and cut out the bridge between them with a jigsaw. With the divider option the crate gets two compartments, for example for bottles and glasses or for two plants.

Decorating ideas

The crate only looks authentic with some patina. Round over the edges with sandpaper, darken the wood with antique stain, coffee or a blowtorch and then sand lightly. Stencil on some lettering or a crest with acrylic paint for the typical winery look.

  • Planter: line it with pond liner or dimpled membrane and drill a few holes in the bottom.
  • Table centrepiece: fill with moss, fir sprigs, pine cones and candles in glasses.
  • Gift box: bed wine, deli treats or homemade goodies in wood wool.
  • Shelf: screw several crates to the wall on their side, or stack them.

Which timber is best?

Planed pine or spruce is light, cheap and takes stain well. Real wine crates are often pine or poplar. Oak looks high quality but is harder to nail and much more expensive. For planters outdoors, larch is the better choice.

Frequently asked questions

What size is a wine crate?
A crate for six bottles is around 50 × 33 × 18 cm, for example. For one bottle a narrow box of about 35 × 12 × 12 cm is enough. For the size you enter, the calculator shows how many bottles fit lying in one layer.
How much timber do I need for a wine crate?
For a crate of 50 × 33 × 18 cm you need about 4 metres of 90 × 10 mm board for the sides and bottom, plus two end pieces of 31 × 17 cm from an 18 mm board. The material costs very little.
Nails or screws?
Real wine crates are nailed. With panel pins and a little wood glue the crate holds well, and the nail heads are part of the look. If you prefer screws, pre-drill the thin boards so they do not split.
Can I use the crate as a planter?
Yes. Line it, drill drainage holes in the bottom and stand it on small feet or battens so water can drain. Outdoors, larch lasts longer than spruce.

All timber sections are guide values and do not replace a structural calculation. Carports and patio covers may need planning permission and building regulations approval, and a structural engineer's check depending on where you live.
